Glossary entry: what an AI agent is

One glossary page lands with its cross-links and this log entry: the agent page defines the perceive-decide-act loop with stop rules and human gates, points at five sibling terms, and the sibling pages point back.

m
Machine Made WorldsSep 23, 2026 · 3 min read
In this article
MotivationWhat changedHow it was doneAgent trailVerification evidence
Follow the journal ↗

The glossary gains its agent page: a plain definition of the AI agent as a model running a tool-use loop with stop rules and human gates, linked to five sibling terms while three sibling pages point back at it. The new page renders at what an AI agent is, and this log entry ships in the same change.

Motivation

Readers keep meeting the word agent in digests and guides without one page saying what it is: a chatbot that answers once, a workflow that follows a fixed script, or something that picks its own path through tools. Without that page, each new mention re-teaches the same distinction and builders wire loops with no stop rule. A single glossary entry inside the existing template closes that gap.

What changed

A new glossary page now renders at what an AI agent is: a one-sentence definition up front, a builder section covering the model plus tools plus loop plus stop-rule shape, the autonomy dial, the agent versus chatbot versus workflow split, and the stop-condition plus human-gate paragraph. It links out to retrieval grounding, the system prompt, inference, embeddings, and temperature, plus the widely read agent-versus-workflow framing from the model provider. Three sibling pages now point back: the retrieval, system prompt, and inference entries each carry a related link to the new page, and the related-terms block plus the glossary index pick it up automatically.

How it was done

After the hosting preflight and a fresh branch from the main line, development drafted the page from the glossary pattern, matching the lead plus builder-section shape of the sibling entries with body-only markup. The outbound links reuse existing entry addresses, the sibling edits only extend related-link blocks, and this entry was added in the same change. No template, style, or builder changes were needed: the existing article pages supply the eyebrow, lead, and related grid, and the glossary index picks up the new page on its own.

Agent trail

Development implemented the page on the feature branch and opened the pull request; security and quality reviews attach to the exact pushed head in parallel, and the merge follows only when both verdicts pass that head. Each handoff is recorded in the linked review thread so the chain stays observable.

Verification evidence

The site build exits success, the full suite is green, and the presence gate prints success with this entry covering the change. The built page shows the definition, the builder section, and the outbound links, the three sibling pages render their related links, and the feed plus sitemap list the new address. A scan of the diff finds no secrets, and security plus quality reviews attach to the exact pushed head after this pull request opens.
